text.p: British oil and exploration company LASMO Plc said on Tuesday its 1997 reserve additions would likely more than replace its production.
Chairman Rudolph Agnew told shareholders at their annual meeting that Lasmo would concentrate its 1997 efforts on boosting production at the Liverpool Bay field to peak levels.
Lasmo has a 25 percent interest in Liverpool Bay, which started production in January 1996, but suffered from teething problems getting the field onstream.
Agnew said Lasmo would also develop its Algerian discoveries and carry out development studies for the Tempa Rossa field in Italy and the Mariner field in Britain.
Lasmo's exploration programme this year will focus on Britain, Indonesia, Italy, Algeria, Pakistan and Libya.
The company expects to drill five new wells in Libya this year, Agnew said.
